steps.title: Prepare M‑buffer (pH 5.4)
steps.instruction: Mix 20 mL of 0.2 M Na₂HPO₄ (prepared by dissolving 0.852 g in 30 mL water) with 14 mL of 0.1 M citrate (prepared by dissolving 0.576 g in 30 mL water) to obtain M‑buffer at pH 5.4; no further pH adjustment is required.

steps.title: Make active GCase buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve one Roche cOmplet mini protease‑inhibitor tablet in 10 mL of the M‑buffer, add Triton X‑100 to a final concentration of 0.25 % v/v (e.g., 25 µL Triton X‑100 per 10 mL buffer), and add sodium taurocholate to a final concentration of 0.2 % (mass/volume). Mix thoroughly to obtain the active GCase buffer.

steps.title: Prepare CBE and carrier solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute 10 mM CBE stock (in DMSO) with the active GCase buffer to obtain a 0.8 mM CBE solution using a buffer‑to‑CBE volume ratio of 92:8 (i.e., 8 % DMSO final). Prepare a CBE‑free carrier solution of identical composition (GCase buffer:DMSO = 92:8) but without CBE.

steps.title: Arrange plate layout
steps.instruction: Set up a 384‑well flat‑bottom black plate with two sections: one for CBE‑treated wells and one for CBE‑free wells. Plan four replicate wells per sample (protein concentration 0.7–1.2 mg/mL).

steps.title: Dispense protein lysates
steps.instruction: Dilute each protein lysate in the active GCase buffer to achieve ~0.7–1.2 mg/mL, adjust concentrations so control and experimental samples are comparable, and pipette 10 µL of each diluted lysate into the designated wells of the 384‑well plate.

steps.title: Add CBE or carrier
steps.instruction: To the CBE‑positive wells add 5 µL of the 0.8 mM CBE solution; to the CBE‑negative wells add 5 µL of the CBE‑free carrier solution.

steps.title: Incubate with CBE
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with aluminum foil, briefly centrifuge to collect contents, then incubate while shaking at 600 rpm, 37 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare 4‑MU substrate
steps.instruction: Dilute 1 M 4‑Methylumbelliferyl‑B‑D‑glucoside stock (338 mg dissolved in 1 mL DMF) with the active GCase buffer to a final concentration of 2.5 mM (1:400 dilution). This will be used as the assay buffer.

steps.title: Add substrate assay buffer
steps.instruction: After the CBE incubation, spin the plate down and add 15 µL of the 2.5 mM 4‑MU assay buffer to each well, bringing the total well volume to 30 µL.

steps.title: Incubate substrate reaction
steps.instruction: Cover the plate with aluminum foil, briefly centrifuge, then incubate while shaking at 450 rpm, 37 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Prepare stop solution
steps.instruction: Make stop solution by adding 4 mL of 5 M NaOH and 1.877 g glycine to water and bringing the final volume to 25 mL; the resulting glycine concentration is 1 M (pH 10.5).

steps.title: Terminate reaction
steps.instruction: After the 1‑hour incubation, spin the plate down again and add 30 µL of the stop solution to each well.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Read 4‑MU fluorescence on a microplate reader using excitation 365 nm, emission 449 nm, cutoff 435 nm, recording three reads per well.
